header: L13 · The reader who holds the spec against itself · opus
verdict: Met for round 10: all five L13 findings with status A (R10-1 to R10-5) read at d133542 as their resolutions say. The largest gap is new and comes from the G5 package split. 05 5.3 and 12 12.4 make `pr` a main package of its own, `tools/ci/pr`, whose import closure is the standard library plus paths on `approvals`. But 12 12.4 still puts `approvalLine` in `tools/ci/askfirst.go`, a file of the `tools/ci` main package, which Go cannot import. 12 12.2 still gives `go run ./tools/ci pr` as the command, and 02 2.1 still lays `tools/ci` out as one dispatcher with one package per step. The closure also leaves out the YAML library of 12 12.1, yet `pr` reads three YAML files that other tools read with that library. Two Required findings and two Advisory ones.

findings.section: 05 5.3 (the `pr` package paragraph; the `approvals` globs); 12 12.4 ("`approvalLine` in `tools/ci/askfirst.go`"; "Where this specification writes `tools/ci pr`"); 12 12.2 (Development commands, the two PR checks lines); 02 2.1 (the `tools/ci/` line); 10 10.2 (steps table, the pr row)
findings.defect: The delta moves `pr` into a main package of its own, `tools/ci/pr`, whose import closure may hold only the standard library and paths on `approvals`. The texts that place its code were left as they were. 12 12.4 defines the approval-line regexp `approvalLine` in `tools/ci/askfirst.go`, and the `approvals` glob names that file. It belongs to package `tools/ci`, the main package that `go run ./tools/ci <subcommand>` builds, and Go refuses to import a main package, so the check `pr` exists to run cannot be in `pr`'s closure. 12 12.2 still gives `go run ./tools/ci pr <payload file>` and `go run ./tools/ci pr --title <t> --body <file>`, while 10 10.2's grammar and local-run paragraph say `go run ./tools/ci/pr`. The alias sentence of 12 12.4 renames the name `tools/ci pr`, not a literal command line. 02 2.1 says `tools/ci` is one package per step under `tools/ci/internal/<step>/` behind a generated dispatcher, and it does not mention the second main package. The `go list -deps` test compares package import paths with `approvals` globs that name single files (`tools/ci/askfirst.go`), and the text does not say how a package is matched against a file glob.
findings.scenario: The task that builds `pr` reads 12 12.4 and writes `approvalLine` in `tools/ci/askfirst.go`, then has `tools/ci/pr` import it. The build fails (`import "…/tools/ci" is a program, not an importable package`). The implementer then copies the check into `tools/ci/pr`, which leaves two approval-line checks: the one on `approvals` is dead, and the one that runs sits on `checks` until the glob change lands. Or the implementer moves it into a `tools/ci/internal/...` package, which is on `checks`, a grantable surface, so the `go list -deps` test fails. Either way, a contributor who pastes the 12 12.2 command runs the dispatcher, which has no `pr` step, or a second `pr` that is not the one the job runs.
findings.change: State one home. The approval-line, grant and forbidden-name checks live under `tools/ci/pr/` (a main package plus, if needed, packages below it), and `approvalLine` is defined there. The `approvals` glob `tools/ci/askfirst.go` becomes `tools/ci/pr/**`, either now or in the tooling pull request that already gains that glob, with the file glob dropped. 12 12.2's two lines become `go run ./tools/ci/pr …`. 02 2.1's `tools/ci/` line names `tools/ci/pr/` as the one main package outside the dispatcher. 05 5.3 says the test maps each package of `go list -deps` to its directory and requires every non-standard package's files to match a glob. Cost: about five sentences on four pages; approval lines `spec` and, for the glob, `ask-first`.

findings.section: 05 5.3 ("whose import closure is the standard library and paths on `approvals`"); 12 12.1 (libraries: `go.yaml.in/yaml/v3`); 12 12.4 (`pr` reads `.github/ask-first.yaml` at base and head; `docs/grants.yaml`); 12 12.3 (the generator that reads `.github/ask-first.yaml`); 10 10.2 (the forbidden-name check of `pr` and `tools/ci/denylist.yaml`)
findings.defect: `pr` reads three YAML files: `.github/ask-first.yaml` at base and head, `docs/grants.yaml` and `tools/ci/denylist.yaml`. The Go standard library has no YAML decoder, and the one YAML library 12 12.1 names, `go.yaml.in/yaml/v3`, is a module path outside the `approvals` globs. So the closure rule forces `pr` to read YAML with a reader of its own, which no text says. The same files are read with the library by the generator of 12 12.3 (CODEOWNERS, `docs/reference/ask-first.md`, the `mutate` trigger) and by `tools/ci hygiene`. That is one problem, reading the surface list, solved two ways, and nothing holds the two readings equal.
findings.scenario: A pull request writes a glob in `.github/ask-first.yaml` in a form the library accepts and a hand-written subset reader reads differently or rejects: a quoted scalar, a flow list split over two lines, an anchor, or a `#` inside a value. CODEOWNERS and `mutate` then see one surface set, and `pr` sees another, so a line is required for a surface the generator does not list, or not required for one it does. Or the implementer imports the library anyway, the `go list -deps` test fails, and the test is the first place the conflict shows.
findings.change: Choose one reader. Recommended: one strict YAML-subset decoder under `tools/ci/pr/` (on `approvals`), which the generator of 12 12.3 and `hygiene` import too, so the files have one reading. A test fails a committed file the subset does not decode, and fixtures cover each refused form. Alternatively, admit `go.yaml.in/yaml/v3` into the closure by name and add `go.sum`, through its module line, to the grantable inputs the toolchain Deferred row lists. Cost: one paragraph in 05 5.3 or 12 12.4 and one test; approval line `spec`.

findings.defect: The delta made askpass a requirement: 06 6.4 says confirm-on-use 'needs a program `SSH_ASKPASS` can name … installed first', and J1 step 5 says to install one and set `SSH_ASKPASS`. The 05 5.4 row was edited in the same pass and still says `ssh-add -c` 'gives confirm-on-use where an askpass program is installed (macOS ships none)', which reads as optional.
findings.scenario: A reader of the security model takes 05 5.4's conditional form as the rule and skips the askpass install. The outcome without one, still unmeasured until B2, is either a refused signing or a signing with no confirmation. The risk table then claims a mitigation the operator was not told to install.
findings.change: In 05 5.4, write 'which gives confirm-on-use through the askpass program J1 step 5 installs (macOS ships none)'. Cost: one clause; approval line `spec`.

findings.defect: The narrowed row reads 'a sandbox a project names with no open generation, a generation in `removing` excluded'. It can be read two ways: as removing the case from the check, which the resolution of L13-R10-4 means, or as leaving a `removing` generation out of the open generations counted, which makes the row match the very case `removal-pending` now owns. 01 1.7 already says `removing` is not open outside `rm`, `recreate` and `retire`.
findings.scenario: The doctor task takes the second reading and reports a removing generation with its sandbox present as both `generation-sandbox` and `removal-pending`, each with a different hint.
findings.change: Write 'a sandbox a project names with no generation in `open`, `salvaging` or `removing`'. Cost: one clause.

confidence: High for L13-R11-1: Go's rule that a main package cannot be imported, and the quoted 12 12.2, 12 12.4 and 02 2.1 lines at d133542, settle it. High for L13-R11-2 on the facts. The severity depends on whether the implementer would have chosen the library, which the closure test then fails. High that the five round-10 resolutions hold, each read in place.
